title: AI Is Making a Mess of Nurses’ Schedules. They Say It’s a Safety Issue
gist: HCA Healthcare's Palantir-built AI scheduling tool Timpani, deployed at about 130 of 190 hospitals, is blamed by nurses for understaffing, ignored preferences and safety risks, while HCA claims large efficiency gains. The piece also notes Palantir's quarterly sales near $2 billion and similar problems at Rayus Radiology.

insights.claim: HCA has deployed Timpani, an AI nurse-scheduling tool co-developed with Palantir since 2023, at roughly 130 of its 190 locations.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Shows how fast Palantir's commercial footprint is spreading in the largest US hospital chain.

insights.claim: Timpani is built on Palantir Foundry and uses algorithmic forecasts of patient volumes and staffing needs to auto-build nursing schedules.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Foundry as a platform layer lets Palantir expand from data integration into workflow automation inside regulated industries.
insights.locator: Timpani was built on Palantir Foundry

insights.claim: HCA's innovation chief claims Timpani cuts manager scheduling hours, reduces reliance on costly contract nurses and boosts retention, with over 98 percent of schedules mixing skill levels.
insights.speaker: Michael Schlosser, HCA
insights.so_what: Labor-cost savings, especially lower contract-nurse spend, are the ROI pitch driving hospital AI adoption, and nurses' accounts contradict it.
insights.quote: The efficiency comes from AI generating stronger initial schedules
insights.locator: Schlosser said in a paper this past July

insights.claim: HCA says Timpani schedules nurses on only 1 percent of requested days off, yet nurses say assignment on such days was previously unheard of, and that essentially every nurse at one Missouri facility has been scheduled on a day off.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Aggregate AI performance metrics can hide a change in worker experience that drives attrition and labor friction.

insights.claim: Nurses allege Timpani causes understaffed, imbalanced and exhausted care teams, especially too few veteran nurses and too few staff on Sundays, with minimal oversight.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Patient-safety liability and regulatory scrutiny are the tail risk for AI workforce automation in healthcare.
insights.locator: The nurses who spoke with WIRED allege

insights.claim: Schedule appeals now go to a centralized HCA team in Nashville with no direct communication, and nurses claim shift-swap success is only about 50 percent, removing local manager discretion.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Centralising decisions in algorithms strips local judgment, creating friction costs that offset efficiency gains.
insights.locator: Initially, some local managers could edit

insights.claim: National Nurses United, representing about 10,000 of HCA's 100,000 nurses, says HCA rejected its information requests, and a 500-nurse psychiatric center union filed a grievance likely headed to arbitration.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Organised labor is becoming the main check on workplace AI in healthcare, creating legal and cost risk.

insights.claim: A former HCA data science manager sued in July 2026, alleging retaliatory firing after raising concerns that HCA routinely deletes data Timpani uses, which prevents auditing and may violate healthcare laws.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Auditability of AI systems is emerging as a litigation vector; HCA has yet to formally respond.
insights.locator: Some purported details emerged in July

insights.claim: Nurses at an HCA psychiatric center claim colleagues quit and workplace injuries rose during the first 12 months of Timpani.
insights.speaker: Lee Barker, HCA nurse
insights.so_what: Attrition claims, if borne out, undercut HCA's retention rationale and add staffing costs.
insights.locator: Barker, who is a National Nurses United leader

insights.claim: Palantir's sales have nearly doubled to almost $2 billion per quarter, with soaring costs and staffing shortages making healthcare providers especially eager customers.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Healthcare labor scarcity is a durable demand driver for Palantir's commercial AI platform.
insights.quote: Palantir’s sales have nearly doubled recently to almost $2 billion per quarter

insights.claim: Palantir has a $440 million NHS contract to cut appointment wait times, but UK nurses and activists demand cancellation over privacy and security concerns.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Large public health contracts carry political-reversal risk for Palantir.

insights.claim: A Palantir Foundry tool at Rayus Radiology linked orders to wrong patient profiles, listed mismatched scans and invented patient details, with schedulers blaming nonstandard forms and insufficient human review.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Hallucination-like errors in medical workflows raise liability risk for AI deployments, and Palantir says customers own data and decisions.
insights.locator: Rayus Radiology, a large US imaging chain

insights.claim: Palantir frames its software as presenting information more helpfully and says customers are responsible for data, policies and decisionmaking, which shifts liability to clients.
insights.speaker: Palantir spokesperson
insights.so_what: The liability-allocation stance is a key legal moat question as AI errors surface in regulated sectors.
insights.locator: A Palantir spokesperson declined to comment
